notes:
I found plenty of traditional commentary, almost all of it about names, family lines and copying errors. I didn't find any verse in this passage where Protestant traditions actually disagree, and I found no Catholic, Orthodox, Bible Odyssey, NET Bible study note or popular-teaching (prosperity and the like) material on it. Those categories are left out below. Note that the older commentaries number the verses as the KJV does, which differs slightly from the BSB in vv. 25–27.

**Overview (vv. 1–27)**
- Guzik: the chapter traces Levi and Aaron. All priests were therefore Levites, but not all Levites were priests. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-chronicles-4-8/
- Matthew Henry: priests and Levites had to keep their family records clear because all the honours and privileges of their office depended upon their descent. He points to Ezra 2:62–63, where men who couldn't prove their descent were barred from the priesthood. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
- Constable: the list seems meant to legitimate and clarify their role and service in the temple. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/1-chronicles/6-10.html

**v. 1:** The Pulpit Commentary says the three branches of Levi match Genesis 46:11 and Exodus 6:16. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 2:** Pulpit: Kohath is picked out first because the priestly line runs through him. Kohathites appear in sacred duties under David and Hezekiah. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 3**
- Henry: Moses and Aaron were models of the one to come, Moses as prophet and Aaron as priest. Naming Nadab and Abihu, who had no children, reminds us of God's judgment on their "strange fire," that we may always fear before him. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
- Pulpit: naming Eleazar, Aaron's third son, settles which line the priesthood follows. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 4**
- Pulpit: twenty-two names run from Eleazar to Jehozadak. It treats the claim that the priesthood passed for a time to Ithamar's family (Eli) as somewhat unclear, and calls Phinehas a memorable man (Num 25; Ps 106:30–31). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm
- Henry: not everyone named here was high priest. The office moved to Ithamar's family (Eli's) during the judges and in Zadok it returned again to the right line. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm

**vv. 5–7**
- JFB: some think that under Uzzi the high priesthood moved to Ithamar's family for unrecorded reasons. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
- Pulpit: Bukki through Amariah reappear in Ezra 7, but little else is known about them. There may have been unnamed high priests in the gap before Eli. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 8:** Pulpit: from Ahitub on, the names are well known from Samuel and Kings. Zadok joined David at Hebron and stayed loyal when Abiathar sided with Adonijah. Pulpit thinks Zadok died before the temple was dedicated. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**vv. 9–10 (the most discussed verses)**
The question is which Azariah "served as priest in the temple Solomon built."
- **Moved from v. 9:** Barnes says the note must belong to the earlier Azariah (v. 9), because Zadok cannot have been succeeded by a great-great-grandson. Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary agree and blame a copyist. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-10.htm and https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **Opposed King Uzziah:** Henry, Clarke and the Geneva notes link it to the Azariah who stood against Uzziah's attempt to burn incense (2 Chr 26:17–18). Henry adds that Urijah, who gave in to King Ahaz, may have been left out of the list as a disgrace. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/1-chronicles/6-10.html
- **Undecided:** JFB says it could refer to Johanan, if he is the same man as Jehoiada (2 Kgs 11), or to Azariah. Both JFB and Poole say "Solomon's temple" is named this way to tell it apart from the second temple. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-10.htm
- **Keil and Delitzsch** reject the transposition theory and conclude that some known high priests are missing from the list. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-10.htm
- **Applying it to Christ:** the Bible Hub study notes call the priesthood a type of Christ, our final High Priest (Heb 5:1). https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6-10.htm

**v. 11:** Pulpit: this Amariah was high priest under King Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 19:11). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 12:** Pulpit: the second Ahitub–Zadok pair may be a copying error, though it could be genuine. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 13:** Pulpit: Shallum is the Meshullam of 1 Chr 9:11. Hilkiah is famous for finding the Book of the Law, backing Josiah's reforms, and the great Passover. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 14:** Pulpit: Seraiah was high priest under Zedekiah and was killed by the Babylonians (2 Kgs 25:18–21). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm

**v. 15**
- Guzik: even in this disaster the writer saw God's hand. The LORD, not Babylon, sent Judah away. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-chronicles-4-8/
- Ellicott: the Chronicler is often accused of a priestly bias, but this verse fits the outlook of the great prophets. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- Pulpit: Jehozadak never became high priest and lived out his life in captivity. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm
- Henry: the priestly line was left where it was found, which hints that the Levitical priesthood made nothing perfect. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm

**vv. 16–19**
- JFB: the list repeats here because it now turns to the Levite families who were not priests. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
- Pulpit: the names agree with Exodus 6 and Numbers 3. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm
- Ellicott (v. 19): "families" means clans, not single households. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html

**vv. 20–21**
- JFB: "Zimmah his son" means his grandson (v. 42). https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
- Pulpit: it's unclear how this list relates to Asaph's line (vv. 39–43). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/1_chronicles/6.htm
- Henry says this Gershom line runs down to Samuel. That conflicts with vv. 22–27 and the other sources, which put Samuel under Kohath. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm

**v. 22**
- **Amminadab:** Gill and the Geneva notes say Amminadab is the same person as Izhar. Ellicott thinks Izhar's name more likely dropped out of the text. Keil discusses both explanations. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-22.htm
- **Korah:** the Bible Hub notes say the rebel Korah's descendants became psalm-writers, a picture of God's grace. https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6-22.htm

**v. 23:** Ellicott and Keil: Assir, Elkanah and Ebiasaph were probably brothers, and the second Assir was Ebiasaph's son. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-22.htm

**v. 24:** JFB: Uriel is the Zephaniah of v. 36. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm Keil thinks the two lines split after Tahath. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-22.htm

**vv. 25–26**
- Ellicott: the extra "Elkanah" in the Hebrew of v. 26 is an intrusion. Ahimoth may be the Mahath of v. 35. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-26.htm
- Keil: the traditional Hebrew text here is Beyond doubt corrupt. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-26.htm
- Benson and Poole: Nahath is the Toah of v. 34 and the Tohu of 1 Sam 1:1. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-26.htm
- NET Bible dictionary: Zophai is the same as Zuph. Budde and Wellhausen instead read 1 Sam 1:1 as "a Zuphite." https://classic.net.bible.org/dictionary.php?word=ZOPHAI

**v. 27**
- **Samuel's father:** JFB says this Elkanah is the father of the prophet Samuel. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm Ellicott thinks the words "Samuel his son" may have dropped out after this verse. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **Levite or Ephraimite?** 1 Sam 1:1 calls Elkanah an Ephraimite. Constable explains he was an Ephraimite by residence but a Levite by birth. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/1-samuel/1-1.html Keil (on 1 Sam 1:1) adds that leaving Samuel's Levite descent unmentioned there is no valid objection. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_samuel/1-1.htm
- **Was Samuel a priest?** Ligonier (Reformed) notes that Ramathaim-Zophim was not a Levite town. Scripture never directly calls Samuel a priest, though Psalm 99:6 lists him alongside Moses and Aaron. https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/difference-between-levitical-and-aaronic-priesthood Precept Austin quotes a view that Samuel was effectively adopted into a Levitical line. https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-samuel-1-commentary
